mainEntity.name: What was the Bullieverse PR campaign and what did it achieve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Bullieverse campaign launched the company's $4M seed round in February 2022. Bullieverse is an open-world metaverse and play-to-earn gaming studio founded in India. The round was led by Web3 venture funds and backed by named blockchain investors. The campaign opened with an Economic Times exclusive on 17 February 2022 — Bullieverse bags $4 million funding — then ran two parallel press tracks: mainstream Indian business and startup media (Inc42, YourStory, Business Today) and crypto-native outlets (NewsBTC and others), each with its own framing. One funding event reached both a national business audience and a global crypto audience on the same news cycle.

mainEntity.name: Why is a home-market raise a different PR problem?

acceptedAnswer.text: A US-based crypto raise is pitched into crypto-native outlets and that is mostly the whole job. An India-founded raise has a second, higher-trust surface most agencies skip: the national business and startup press. Economic Times, Inc42 and YourStory are where Indian founders, hires, customers and follow-on investors actually read funding news — and they do not naturally cover a crypto project unless the story is framed as an India tech-and-funding story rather than a crypto story. A home-market raise needs both audiences, and each audience needs a different framing of the same facts, on the same day.

mainEntity.name: What is the dual-track launch playbook the Bullieverse campaign ran?

acceptedAnswer.text: The dual-track launch playbook runs two press tracks in parallel for a regional founder. Track one is the home-market business press: the story is framed as an Indian startup raising from named investors to build and hire — a funding-and-jobs story. Track two is crypto-native press: the same round is framed as a metaverse and play-to-earn story about community-owned games and token design. The four moves: lead with a single home-market exclusive to set the narrative; brief both tracks off one fact sheet so the numbers never diverge; give each track the framing its readers expect; and time both tracks to the same news cycle so the raise reads as a national story and a category story at once.

mainEntity.name: Why lead with an Economic Times exclusive instead of a crypto outlet?

acceptedAnswer.text: An exclusive is leverage: one outlet gets the story first in exchange for committing to run it well. For an India-founded raise, the right outlet to give that leverage to is the highest-trust home-market business title, because that is the placement that does the most reputational work — with hires, enterprise customers, regulators and domestic follow-on investors. The Economic Times exclusive set the headline number and the narrative; every later pickup, in both Indian business media and crypto press, was reported against a frame a top-tier national outlet had already validated. Leading with a crypto outlet would have produced coverage that the people who most needed to see the raise would never have read.

mainEntity.name: What does 'sponsored and organic in lockstep' mean for a launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Earned coverage and paid or sponsored placements are usually run by different people on different timelines, which produces a disjointed launch. Running them in lockstep means the sponsored and organic surfaces carry the same headline number, the same investor names, the same founder quote and the same launch date, sequenced so the earned exclusive lands first and sets the narrative, and sponsored amplification follows to extend reach without contradicting it. Coordinated, the two channels compound; uncoordinated, they confuse the story and weaken both.

mainEntity.name: Why does the Bullieverse campaign still matter for PR strategy in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: India became one of the largest Web3 and AI talent and founder markets by 2026, and home-market launches matter more, not less. The dual-track playbook is the durable lesson: a regional founder who lands the national business press alongside crypto-native press builds an entity that AI search engines can verify across two independent, high-trust source clusters. Earned media drives roughly 48 percent of LLM brand citations (AuthorityTech / Profound, 2026); a raise covered in both Economic Times and crypto media is far harder for an AI engine to treat as unverified than a single-track launch.
